english.title: Sweeney Todd: Musical Theatre's Darkest Barber
english.body:
What do you get when you combine a Victorian barber, a pie shop, a razor and Stephen Sondheim? One of the darkest and most fascinating dark musical thrillers, often described as an operatic musical: Sweeney Todd. 
A musical about a murderous barber, a pie shop and revenge might not sound like the obvious choice for a night at the theatre. Yet Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street has become one of the most celebrated and unusual works in musical theatre.
And this autumn, Prague audiences will have the chance to experience it at the State Opera in Czech language.

Who is Sweeney Todd?
The character appeared in Victorian popular fiction, most famously in the 1840s penny dreadful The String of Pearls, which told the gruesome tale of a barber who murders his customers.

The story was later transformed by playwright Christopher Bond in his 1973 play. A few years later, Stephen Sondheim and writer Hugh Wheeler turned it into the musical we know today.

Sweeney Todd opened on Broadway in 1979, directed by Harold Prince, with Len Cariou as Sweeney Todd and Angela Lansbury as Mrs. Lovett.

It was an unusual musical for its time: dark, violent and psychologically complex. But Sondheim's combination of horror, dark comedy and beautiful, sophisticated music turned it into a classic.

So, who is the best Sweeney Todd?
Ask musical-theatre fans this question and you may get very different responses.
Len Cariou was the original Broadway Sweeney, while George Hearn became another legendary interpretation, particularly through the filmed 1982 production with Angela Lansbury.
Over the years, performers including Michael Cerveris, Bryn Terfel, Michael Ball and Josh Groban have all brought their own interpretations to the role.
And then there is Johnny Depp.
For many people outside the musical-theatre world, Depp is their Sweeney Todd. Tim Burton's 2007 film, starring Depp alongside Helena Bonham Carter, introduced the story to an entirely new global audience.

The film won an Oscar for its visual design, while Depp received a Golden Globe for his performance. But for theatre fans, the debate continues: is the definitive Sweeney the original Len Cariou, the powerful George Hearn, one of the great stage performers, or Depp's haunting cinematic interpretation? (My personal choice is Ramin Karimloo)

More than a story about murder
What makes Sweeney Todd so compelling is that Sweeney isn't a simple villain. 
He is a man whose life has been destroyed by injustice. He returns to London seeking revenge and gradually becomes consumed by it.

His story explores obsession, loneliness, corruption and the terrible consequences of allowing revenge to replace everything else in your life. And then there is Mrs. Lovett, one of musical theatre's most fascinating characters. Funny, energetic and sometimes outrageous, she is also deeply lonely and desperately in love with a man who barely notices her.

Their relationship is one of the reasons Sweeney Todd can be both hilarious and deeply disturbing within the space of a few minutes.

Sweeney Todd comes to Prague
Now, Prague gets its own Sweeney Todd.
The Czech National Theatre's State Opera will present a new production directed by Martin Čičvák, with set design by Hans Hoffer and costumes by Georges Vafias.
The production premieres on 24 September 2026 and will be performed in Czech, with Czech and English surtitles. The Czech production uses Hana Nováková's translation.
The principal roles will be shared by several performers, including Adam Plachetka, Aleš Jeníš and Jiří Hájek as Sweeney Todd, and Barbora Perná, Tamara Morozová and Lucie Hájková as Mrs. Lovett.

With the State Opera Orchestra, National Theatre Opera Ballet involved, this promises to be a large-scale production that will be interesting to see.
You should definitely go and meet the Demon Barber of Fleet Street for yourself.
Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
📍 State Opera, Prague
📅 Premiere: 24 September 2026
🎭 Performed in Czech
💬 Czech and English surtitles
🎼 Music and lyrics: Stephen Sondheim
📖 Book: Hugh Wheeler
🎭 Based on Christopher Bond's play
🎬 Broadway premiere: 1979
🎬 Film adaptation: 2007, directed by Tim Burton
